description: Last in, first out. `push` and `pop` on the end of an array are O(1). Used for rollbacks, undo and depth-first traversal.
First in, first out. Items leave in arrival order. Used for job queues, buffering and breadth-first traversal.
A pointer to the next item to dequeue, so removing from the front does not move every other element as `shift()` does.
The `down` of a step: what undoes it when a later step fails. Run in reverse order, it forms a saga across services.
Slowing or rejecting producers when consumers fall behind, so a buffer does not grow until memory runs out.
A queue stored outside the process (Redis, Postgres, SQS) that survives restarts and is shared between instances.
